title: Up Longer? Time of Flight Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A high kick hangs in the air for ages, a flat throw lands almost at once. Aarav throws a ball at 30°, then at 60°, with the same speed. Which one stays up longer? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we find out exactly what decides the time of flight.

Two balls fly side by side in a live simulation with two clocks and a height-time graph, plus a slow-motion replay at the top that shows going up takes as long as coming down. We derive T = 2v₀ sin θ / g step by step, check it a second way through the top of the path, and see why the sideways speed never changes the time. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example, the forgotten-2 exam trap and an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A high kick, a flat throw, a puddle jump
0:26 What is the time of flight?
0:44 Live sim: 30° vs 60° at the same speed, slow-mo at the top
1:21 Deriving T = 2v₀ sin θ / g, step by step
2:04 A second way: time to the top, then double it
2:26 30° vs 60° side by side + pause and think
3:02 No cos θ: drop vs push off a table
3:31 Worked example: 19.6 m/s at 30°
3:57 Exam trap: forgetting the 2
4:18 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:59 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Maximum Height. The ball turns around at half its flight time, but how high is that turning point?
